ledger_validation: All captured and final valid histories have contiguous 1-based integer seq, correct provider/version/domain-separated recomputed hashes/links, no duplicate authorization IDs, matching snapshots. S02 intentionally invalid ledgers preserved unmodified.

snapshot_reconciliation.actual_implementation: Any readable JSON snapshot unequal to the ledger-derived document is replaced from ledger and logged as mismatch_or_stale. No distinction among behind, ahead, divergent or malformed-structure snapshots; missing/malformed/unreadable snapshots also trigger rebuild.
snapshot_reconciliation.ahead_or_divergent_snapshot: NOT_FAIL_CLOSED; replaced if ledger validates. This is implemented by both reviewed runtimes. R2 exercised older S0 only, not ahead/divergent cases.
snapshot_reconciliation.implication: Rolling back only the ledger while retaining an ahead snapshot can discard the snapshot evidence of later consumes; this behavior is broader than snapshot-only recovery and must be explicitly reviewed before freeze. No new runtime experiment was executed.

limitations: No resistance to rolling back BOTH ledger and snapshot to older mutually consistent history.
S01/S02 raw console + matching source support pre-listener startup failure; socket-probe result and exit code are recorded only as harness assertions, not standalone raw probe artifacts.
S03 preserved S0, preserved L1 and recovery output support snapshot-only rollback; no separate capture of on-disk replaced S0 immediately before restart.
R2 environment binds runtime identities but does not independently record a full executed harness hash inventory.
Durable fsync-before-START ordering is confirmed statically in matching provider code; evidence is not an OS syscall trace or power-loss/crash-window experiment.
